{{Short description|French mathematical physicist}}
[[File:Vincent Rivasseau.jpg|thumb|Vincent Rivasseau at the [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach|MFO]], 2006]]
'''Vincent Rivasseau''' (born 5 December 1955 in [[Talence]]) is a French mathematical physicist.

Rivasseau studied from 1974 to 1978 at the [[École Normale Supérieure]] and then in 1978/79 at [[Princeton University]] with [[Arthur Wightman]] as advisor. In 1979 he got  his  PhD (Thèse de troisième cycle, Sommations et Estimations d'amplitudes de Feynman),
at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]], followed by the Thèse d'État (1982, Développements asymptotiques et méthodes graphiques en physique mathématique). From 1981 to 2001 he was a scientist of the [[CNRS]] at the 
Center for Theoretical Physics of [[École Polytechnique]]. Since 2001 he is professor of physics at the [[University of Paris-Sud]] in [[Orsay]].

Rivasseau's research deals with [[constructive quantum field theory]] and renormalization theory<ref>{{citation
|url=http://press.princeton.edu/titles/4847.html
|title=From Perturbative to Constructive Renormalization
|last=Rivasseau
|first=Vincent
|date=1991}}</ref> with applications to many-body theory, such as quantum interacting [[fermions]] in solid state physics.<ref>{{citation
|arxiv=1112.5104
|title=Introduction to the Renormalization Group with Applications to Non-Relativistic Quantum Electron Gases
|last=Rivasseau
|first=Vincent
|date=24 February 2011|bibcode=2012AIPC.1444...18R
|doi=10.1063/1.4715396
}}</ref> Since 2004 he has studied quantum field theories on noncommutative space-time,<ref>{{citation
|arxiv=0705.0705
|chapter=Non-commutative Renormalization
|last=Rivasseau
|first=Vincent
|date=4 May 2007|bibcode=2007rqft.book..271R
|doi=10.1007/978-3-7643-7434-1_19
|title=Rigorous Quantum Field Theory
|volume=251
|pages=271–281
|series=Progress in Mathematics
|isbn=978-3-7643-7433-4
}}</ref>
then group field theory. Since 2011 he develops the tensor track<ref>{{citation
|arxiv=1112.5104
|title=Quantum Gravity and Renormalization: The Tensor Track
|journal=American Institute of Physics Conference Series
|volume=1444
|issue=1
|pages=18–29
|last=Rivasseau
|first=Vincent
|date=21 December 2011|bibcode=2012AIPC.1444...18R
|doi=10.1063/1.4715396
|series=AIP Conference Proceedings
}}</ref> approach to quantum gravity 
based on random tensors<ref>{{citation
|url=https://global.oup.com/academic/product/random-tensors-9780198787938?cc=fr&lang=en&
|title=Random Tensors
|last=Gurau
|first=Razvan
|date=October 2016}}</ref>
(higher-dimensional generalizations of random matrices).

From 2000 to 2012 he was editor in chief of [[Annales Henri Poincaré]] [https://www.springer.com/birkhauser/physics/journal/23] and is 
currently co-editor in chief of Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincaré D [http://www.ems-ph.org/journals/journal.php?jrn=AIHPD].

He is committed to the development of science in Africa, being a co-founder of the AIMS-Sénégal Institute  [http://www.aims-senegal.org/] (2011)<ref>{{cite news
|url=http://www.universityworldnews.com/article.php?story=20110507092354899
|title=Senegal: Second postgraduate maths institute to open}}
</ref> and 
former president of the Association pour la Promotion Scientifique de l'Afrique [http://www.scienceafrique.fr/], which he founded in 2009. He is also co-organizer of the [[Poincaré Seminars]]
[http://www.bourbaphy.fr/] at the [[Institut Henri Poincaré]].
